Here's a comprehensive breakdown of the **Women's Team Archery event at the 2012 London Summer Olympics**, based on official records, historical data, and key details:

---

### **1. Event Basics**
- **Official Name**: Archery – Women's Team
- **Dates**: August 2–3, 2012
- **Venue**: Lord's Cricket Ground (London, England)  
  *Note: A temporary archery range was built on the historic cricket pitch, with the iconic Lord's Pavilion as a backdrop.*
- **Format**: Recurve archery only (standard for Olympic archery).
- **Teams**: 12 nations qualified (3 archers per team).

---

### **2. Competition Format**
- **Ranking Round**:  
  - All 36 archers (12 teams × 3) shot 72 arrows (18 ends of 4 arrows) at 70 meters.  
  - Team score = sum of individual scores (max 2,160 points).  
  - Determined seeding for the elimination rounds.
- **Elimination Rounds**:  
  - **Match Format**: Best-of-4 sets (first to 5 set points wins).  
  - **Per Set**: Each archer shot 2 arrows (6 total per team); highest cumulative score wins the set (2 points). Tie = 1 point each.  
  - **Shoot-off**: If tied after 4 sets, single-arrow shoot-off (closest to center wins).
- **Bracket**: Top 8 teams from ranking round advanced to head-to-head elimination (1v8, 2v7, etc.).

---

### **3. Key Results & Medalists**
#### **Gold: South Korea**  
- **Team**: Ki Bo-bae, Lee Sung-jin, Choi Hyeon-ju (alternate who did not shoot in finals).  
- **Ranking Round**: **2,087 points** (World Record-equalling score; matched their own 2011 record).  
- **Path to Gold**:  
  - Round of 16: Bye (as #1 seed).  
  - Quarterfinals: Defeated Poland (214–208).  
  - Semifinals: Defeated Italy (213–207).  
  - **Gold Medal Match**: vs. China – **210–209** (nail-biting 1-point victory).  
    - *Sets*: China won Set 1 (55–54), Korea won Sets 2–4 (56–53, 55–54, 55–52).  
- **Historical Significance**:  
  - Korea's **4th consecutive Olympic gold** in women's team archery (since 2000).  
  - Extended their dominance to **5 golds in 7 Olympics** (1988, 2000, 2004, 2008, 2012).

#### **Silver: China**  
- **Team**: Cheng Ming, Fang Yuting, Xu Jing.  
- **Ranking Round**: 2,069 points (2nd seed).  
- **Path to Silver**:  
  - Beat Japan (211–205) and Belarus (212–206) en route to final.  
- **Final**: Pushed Korea to the limit; Xu Jing's final arrow (9) sealed the narrow loss.

#### **Bronze: Italy**  
- **Team**: Natalia Valeeva, Guendalina Sartori, **Jessica Rossi** (who also won **gold in shooting** at these same Olympics!).  
- **Ranking Round**: 2,013 points (5th seed).  
- **Path to Bronze**:  
  - Lost semifinal to Korea (207–213), then beat Belarus **215–212** in bronze match.  
- **Fun Fact**: Jessica Rossi remains the only athlete to win Olympic gold in **two different sports** (shooting: 25m pistol; archery team bronze) at the same Games.

#### **4th Place: Belarus**  
- Team: Katsiaryna Silkina, Dzintra Bluka, Natalia Pretchel.  
- Lost bronze match to Italy after semifinal loss to China.

---

### **4. Notable Details & Records**
- **Ranking Round Standout**:  
  - Korea (2,087) and China (2,069) were far ahead of 3rd-place USA (2,023).  
  - Ki Bo-bae (KOR) led individuals with 666 points, setting an Olympic record.
- **Closest Match**: Gold medal final decided by **1 point** – the narrowest margin in Olympic women's team history at the time.
- **Venue Quirk**: Lord's Cricket Ground hosted archery for the first time; organizers installed grass-covered berms to protect the turf.
- **Korean Dominance**:  
  - Korea swept **all 4 archery golds** available (men's/women's individual and team).  
  - Women's team hadn't lost an Olympic match since 1992.
- **No Major Upsets**: Top 4 seeds (KOR, CHN, ITA, BLR) filled all medal/4th-place spots.

---

### **5. Full Medal Match Scores**
| **Set** | **South Korea** | **China** | **Set Points** |
|---------|-----------------|-----------|---------------|
| 1       | 54             | 55        | CHN 2–0       |
| 2       | 56             | 53        | KOR 2–0 (2–2) |
| 3       | 55             | 54        | KOR 2–0 (4–2) |
| 4       | 55             | 52        | KOR 2–0 (6–2) |
| **TOTAL** | **210**       | **209**   | **KOR 5–3**   |

---

### **6. Why This Event Matters**
- **Peak of Korean Archery**: This victory cemented Korea's status as archery's powerhouse, driven by rigorous training systems and national investment.
- **Historic Venue**: Lord's became one of the most picturesque Olympic archery venues ever.
- **Crossover Stardom**: Jessica Rossi's dual-medal feat highlighted exceptional versatility in precision sports.
- **Legacy**: Korea's winning streak continued until **Rio 2016** (5 straight golds).

For deeper research:  
- [Official London 2012 Archery Report](https://stillmed.olympic.org/media/Document%20Library/OlympicOrg/General/EN-Results-Archery.pdf)  
- [World Archery's 2012 Event Recap](https://worldarchery.org/results-calendar/results/olympic-games/5535-london-2012)
